historical_claims.anchor: First, Davis and Kahan's Proposition 3.2: for an arbitrary pair of closed subspaces, a direct rotation exists if and only if the two defect spaces have the same dimension.
After proving Proposition 3.2, Davis and Kahan adopt a standing convention for the rest of the paper
historical_claims.source_locator: Section 3, standing convention after the proof of Proposition 3.2

historical_claims.anchor: Davis and Kahan's Proposition 3.4 states the general version.
Proposition 3.3 accepts such a square root as a direct rotation exactly when it carries the source defect onto the target defect.

related_resources.reason: The defect subspaces and generic part used to build and parametrize direct rotations.
Survey of two-projection theory, including when two projections are unitarily equivalent and the role of the defect dimensions.
Planar rotations and reflections: the plus-or-minus ninety degree choices and the double-angle composition used here.
